transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because my regular doctor seems concerned that my meal planning has gotten a bit too tight. I don't really see it that way, but... to me, it just feels like keeping things orderly. 

I usually keep breakfast to just a yogurt, and I'll skip lunch if I’m busy with work. Then I just make sure to have a very measured dinner. It really just helps the day stay structured and under control, but she felt strongly that I should come talk to you about it.
Have you experienced any significant weight loss recently?

Well, yes. My weight has drifted down... more than my regular doctor likes, anyway. But honestly, when I look at the chart, I still find myself thinking that getting it a little lower would just be a cleaner, more manageable number.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yes. Honestly, if the scale is up even just a pound... like after a normal dinner or a restaurant meal... I feel this sharp panic. It just feels like I’ve lost control of things, and I immediately feel the need to correct it the next day.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, feeling like you can't stop?

No, not at all. Um... I don't really have that issue. If anything, it's the exact opposite. I keep everything very measured and planned out. The idea of just eating a large amount of food and not being able to stop... no, I haven't experienced that.
Do you think your weight is currently at a healthy level?

Well, my regular physician tells me it's medically unsafe right now. But... part of me really thinks she’s overstating it. I mean, I'm still working, I run all my own errands, and I manage my life just fine. It's hard for me to see it as a serious health issue when I'm still getting up and doing everything I need to do every day without a problem.
Do you ever feel like you've lost control while you're eating?
No, I don't. Like I said just a moment ago, I really don't have that problem. Everything I eat is very controlled and planned. I never feel like I'm losing control when I'm eating.
Is your fear of gaining weight related to how you think you look?

Yes, I suppose it is. Um... I know I’m an older woman, and I'm really not trying to look young. It's not about that. But... I still judge how well I’m handling myself by whether my waist and hips look contained in my clothes. If they don't, I feel like I'm failing. So, yes, it does come down to my shape and how I look.
Do you think your self-worth is tied to your weight or body shape?

Well, yes, like I was just saying... I think it is. I know I'm 63, and I'm not trying to look like a young woman anymore. But... I really do judge how well I'm doing in life by how my body looks. If my waist and hips don't look contained in my clothes, I feel like I'm not handling myself well. So, yes, my sense of self-worth is definitely tied to my shape.
Do you engage in excessive physical activity to burn off calories?

No, I don't really do that. I mean, I try to stay active just for my general health, but I wouldn't say I exercise excessively or specifically to burn off calories. My control comes more from what I eat, not from working out all the time.
Do you think that if you were to gain weight, you would become fat?

Yes, I do. It's... well, if the scale goes up even a single pound after a normal dinner or eating at a restaurant, I feel this sharp panic. It just makes me feel like I’ve completely lost control and that I'm going to get fat if I don't stop it. So I always feel like I need to correct it the very next day.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No, I don't do that. I've never made myself throw up. Like I said, I just strictly manage what I eat to keep things under control.
Do you think your body image is distorted or not accurate when you look in the mirror?

I don't really think it's distorted, no. I mean, I just see what's there. I know I’m an older woman, and I'm not trying to look young or anything like that. But... I still judge how well I’m handling myself by whether my waist and hips look contained in my clothes. When I look in the mirror, that's mainly what I'm checking. It's just how I measure if I'm keeping things under control.
Do you think you would still want to control your food intake as strictly if you didn't care about your body shape or weight?

I'm not really sure. I suppose... well, it's hard to separate the two in my mind. I've always tied what I eat directly to how my clothes fit and keeping my weight in check. So, if I suddenly just didn't care about my shape at all... I don't know if I would be as strict. I really haven't ever thought about it that way before.
Have you experienced any changes in your menstrual cycle?
Well, I'm 63, so... no. I went through menopause quite a few years ago. I don't really have a menstrual cycle anymore to notice any changes with.
Do you think your strict meal planning is a way to prevent feeling out of control in other areas of your life?

I don't think so. I mean, my job involves a lot of planning and analyzing, so I'm used to having things structured. But I don't feel like my life is out of control. The meal planning is really just about managing my weight and making sure my clothes fit right, like I mentioned. I don't really see it as a way to handle anything else.
Is your goal with eating and weight more about achieving a specific thin body ideal or avoiding being overweight?

It's definitely more about avoiding gaining weight. It's... well, it's a very strong fear for me. If I step on the scale and it's up even a single pound, especially after something like a normal dinner or eating out at a restaurant, I just feel this sharp panic. It feels like I've completely lost control, and I immediately feel like I need to correct it the very next day. So, yes, it's really about making sure the number on the scale doesn't go up.
Are you afraid of gaining weight because of potential health problems it could cause?

No, not really. I mean, I know health is important, especially at my age, but... that's not what I'm thinking about when I step on the scale. When I panic over gaining a pound, I'm not worried about my blood pressure or my joints or anything like that. It's really just the weight itself. I just don't want to get bigger.
Do you avoid eating in front of other people because you're worried about what they might think of your eating habits?

I wouldn't say it's because I'm worried about their opinions. It's really more about the structure. I still keep up with my analysis work and run all my errands without any issues, so I'm out and about. But... well, I’ve mostly stopped joining my friends for meals after our book club. 

It's just that going out to eat throws off the plan I rely on too much. It's much easier for me to just skip the meal with them and stick to what I have planned at home, rather than try to figure out how restaurant food fits into my routine.
Do you feel like you need to continue restricting your food intake to maintain your current weight?

I'm not entirely sure. I haven't really thought about it in those exact terms. I just... I have my daily plan, and I stick to it. I suppose I don't really know what would happen to my weight if I stopped being so careful with my meals. I just know that right now, I don't feel comfortable changing how much I eat.
